name: @concordvoice/media-plane
description: Concord Voice Media Plane - WebRTC SFU for voice routing
author: Concord Voice Team
//overrides_rationale: node-domexception@1.0.0 is deprecated upstream and has no replacement version. fetch-blob@3.x and 4.x both still declare it as a hard dep. We override to a local stub that re-exports globalThis.DOMException (native in Node 18+). Remove this override + the stubs/ directory once mediasoup ships a release pulling node-fetch@^4 stable, OR fetch-blob ships a version that drops the polyfill dep entirely.
//overrides_security: ws@^8.21.3 closes GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (memory-exhaustion DoS; transitive via socket.io->engine.io->ws, vulnerable <8.21.0). Raised from a former ^8.21.0, which sat EXACTLY on that advisory floor with no headroom; socket.io-adapter declares ~8.20.1, which resolves 8.20.1 and is vulnerable, so this override is load-bearing and its one baseline row is deliberate (engine.io declared the same range until 6.6.11, which declares ~8.21.0 and is satisfied, so its row was pruned 2026-09-30). brace-expansion@^5.0.9 closes GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (exponential-time expansion DoS), GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (unbounded expansion -> OOM crash, first patched in 5.0.8 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.3) and GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895 (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays, bypassing the CVE-2026-14257 mitigation; first patched in 5.0.9 on the 5.x line; 2.x at 2.1.4); all three transitive via eslint->minimatch. nanoid@^3.3.17 closes GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 (custom generators loop indefinitely when size is zero; transitive via vite->postcss). socket.io-parser@~4.2.7 closes GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr (zero-attachment memory exhaustion; transitive via socket.io) — this one and ws are the only RUNTIME entries in this block, brace-expansion and nanoid both resolve dev-only. It was reachable pre-auth: the decoder runs on Client.ondata before the namespace auth middleware, so a 0-attachment BINARY_EVENT header installed a reconstructor that never cleared and accumulated buffers unbounded, and maxAttachments does not bound it because that gates the DECLARED count. TILDE, not caret: socket.io declares ~4.2.4, so a caret would force a future 4.3.x wire-format decoder under a socket.io that never declared compatibility with it. Safe here because this package's minimatch (10.2.6) declares brace-expansion ^5.0.8. client/desktop ALSO runs brace-expansion ^5.0.9 now (2026-08-15), having dropped the minimatch@^9 downgrade cap that previously coupled it to the 2.x line; the three workspaces are finally aligned. Read its own //overrides_security note rather than assuming its numbers from here. node-domexception is a file: stub, not a version pin — fetch-blob declares ^1.0.0 and the package is deprecated with no maintained release, so the stub replaces it outright. It is exempt from the override-range lint by design: a stub has no version to compare, so no skew is expressible (see scripts/security/override-range-lint.mjs). These are forced because the intermediates pin older ranges. Drop each override once the parent pulls a patched version natively. VALIDATED 2026-08-15: every entry re-checked against live advisory data and against each consumer's declared range; the only remaining baseline row here is the ws consumer above, forced UPWARD onto a patched version. RAISED 2026-09-30 to brace-expansion@^5.0.12, because three newer advisories on the 4.x/5.x line sit above 5.0.9: GHSA-6j4f-fj2g-mc7p (HIGH, uncontrolled recursion in parseCommaParts, first patched 5.0.10), GHSA-qhr7-859c-m2p7 (HIGH, uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups, first patched 5.0.11) and GHSA-q2hr-2g5m-vwhr (moderate, quadratic-time expansion of the {a},b} rewrite, first patched 5.0.12). 5.0.12 is the newest release and again sits exactly on the newest floor, with zero headroom. Every consumer is minimatch 10.x declaring ^5.0.x, so the raise stays on the declared major and adds no override-range skew. SAME PASS, 2026-09-30: engine.io moved 6.6.8 -> 6.6.11 in the LOCKFILE ONLY, closing GHSA-2gc4-cqfq-p2gv (HIGH, protocol-revision-mismatch DoS; vulnerable >= 6.6.0 < 6.6.10). It is RUNTIME-reachable, since socket.io serves every media-plane connection through it. No override was added, because socket.io declares ~6.6.0 and that range already admits the fix; the npm-audit gate is the control that catches a regression. @babel/core@^7.29.7 was REMOVED in the same pass, as client/desktop removed it in PR #3336: its sole consumer, @vitest/istanbul-lib-instrument, now declares ^8.0.1, so the override had inverted into a DOWNWARD skew holding that consumer a major below its own floor, which is what the governing principle forbids. GHSA-4x5r-pxfx-6jf8, the advisory it existed for, is patched at 8.0.0-rc.6 on the 8.x line, so the 8.0.6 it now resolves clears it unforced. Do not re-add it.
//engines: node's floor was raised from the former >=24.0.0 when #3507 removed the @babel/core override: @babel/core 8.0.6 and the rest of the Babel 8 family it pulls in declare node ^22.18.0 || >=24.11.0, so >=24.0.0 advertised 24.0-24.10 as supported while the coverage toolchain was not. 24.11.0 is the lowest 24.x every locked package accepts. Advisory only - no .npmrc in this repo sets engine-strict - and the runtime image is node:26.
